title: Slow television and the art of watching nothing
text: In 2009, Norwegian broadcasters showed a seven-hour train journey, {{1}} stopping for nothing. Cameras filmed the view from the front of the train, unedited, {{2}} eight hours. Audiences, it turned out, loved it. The genre, known {{3}} 'slow TV', has since included a ferry voyage, a knitting marathon and even the burning of firewood — four hours of a fire, live. Critics assumed nobody would watch; {{4}} , millions did, partly as company, partly as meditation. Slow TV offers {{5}} modern media rarely does: an experience with no highlights reel, {{6}} requires nothing from the viewer. Producers stress that the appeal is not nostalgia {{7}} attention itself. In an age of endless scrolling, simply watching a train pass {{8}} oddly radical.
